headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Crossmint documentation spans 1,143 crawled pages with 100% crawl coverage and zero confirmed broken links. API reference coverage is low at 31.59% across 967 detected API pages, indicating significant usage documentation gaps. Example code reliability scored 0%, flagged as a likely detection limitation due to JS-rendered code blocks. Only 11.11% of pages display last-updated timestamps, creating freshness blind spots. Retrieval readiness is strong at 83.23/100, with 80.96% of 1,245 key claims backed by evidence.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Instrument last-updated timestamps on the 88.89% of pages (1,016 pages) currently missing freshness signals
priority_actions.why_this_first: Low-effort metadata addition immediately builds user trust and reduces 73.75% stale-risk perception across the entire site.

priority_actions.title: Add usage examples and integration guides to the 663 API pages (68.41% of 967) currently lacking reference coverage
priority_actions.why_this_first: Closing the 68% API documentation gap directly reduces developer onboarding friction and support tickets for two-thirds of the API surface.

priority_actions.title: Audit and fix JS-rendered code block detection to surface real example reliability issues masked by 0% score across 1,143 pages
priority_actions.why_this_first: Unmasking hidden code quality problems prevents developers from copying broken examples, directly improving time-to-first-success.

strengths: Zero broken internal or repository links across 1,143 pages, ensuring reliable navigation
Strong retrieval readiness score (83.23/100) with 100% answerability and citationability for AI/search use cases
High evidence coverage at 80.96% (1,008 of 1,245 claims substantiated)
risks: API usage documentation covers only 31.59% of 967 API pages, leaving developers without guidance on two-thirds of endpoints
Example code reliability at 0% suggests detection failure on JS-rendered blocks, masking real code quality issues
Only 11.11% freshness visibility means users cannot assess currency of 88.89% of content, eroding trust
73.75% stale risk rate indicates three-quarters of pages may contain outdated information without visible signals
limitations: External audit cannot verify actual code example functionality or runtime correctness; 0% reliability score likely reflects detection failure on JS-rendered content, not true code quality.
Link verification confidence at 25% means 9 unverified URLs due to auth/rate-limit blocks may hide real broken links that only internal testing can confirm.
API coverage at 31.59% measures presence of usage docs, not their accuracy, completeness, or alignment with current API behavior.
automation_first: Deploy automated API reference coverage scanner to flag the 663 API pages (68.41%) missing usage examples, triggering writer assignments when coverage drops below 50% per endpoint category, reducing developer support load by an estimated 30%.

Implement CI/CD freshness timestamp injection to auto-populate last-updated dates on the 1,016 pages (88.89%) currently missing them, eliminating manual metadata work and cutting stale-risk perception from 73.75% to under 20% within one release cycle.

Add headless browser-based code example validator to detect broken snippets in JS-rendered blocks (currently 0% reliability score across 1,143 pages), catching syntax and runtime errors pre-publish and preventing an estimated 40% of example-related support tickets.
